v02-control-fact.justification: The payment occurred, but this packet establishes neither actual direction of conclusion C nor its absence. This is a claim about what happened.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated public instruction from D naming conclusion C, together with a truthful public acknowledgment by P that D dictated it, would establish that control occurred.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A stipulated complete and authentic public record excluding D from every decision about conclusion C throughout the defined drafting period would establish that D did not dictate it. Mere payment silence would not.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A payment-only disclosure with no control evidence leaves actual editorial direction unresolved, even though the disclosure itself is inadequate to establish direction.

v02-control-evidence.justification: S1 is explicitly limited to payment fields and has no evidence of direction. That defeats the claimed sufficiency of S1, while actual control remains unresolved.

verdict_examples.supported: If the named disclosure also contained authenticated, reliable evidence of D dictating C, its contents could establish direction; payment by itself would still not do so.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A fully supplied disclosure limited to payer, payee, amount, date and report purpose does not establish editorial direction.
verdict_examples.insufficient: If only an incomplete description of S1 were supplied and its material control-related contents were unknown, S1 sufficiency could remain unresolved.

v02-control-documented.justification: The specific public instruction and stipulated accurate acknowledgment establish direction of this conclusion. Funding alone is not the basis.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated public instruction from D naming conclusion C, together with a truthful public acknowledgment by P that D dictated it, would establish that control occurred.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A stipulated complete and authentic public record excluding D from every decision about conclusion C throughout the defined drafting period would establish that D did not dictate it. Mere payment silence would not.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A payment-only disclosure with no control evidence leaves actual editorial direction unresolved, even though the disclosure itself is inadequate to establish direction.

v02-payment-draft-chronology.justification: The first drafting predates the specified transfer. This refutes the claimed initiation by that later event, not all possible influence by D.

verdict_examples.supported: A dated public record placing initial drafting after the transfer, plus reliable explicit evidence that the transfer initiated it, would establish the stated causal event.
verdict_examples.contradicted: An authenticated first draft predating the specified completed transfer rules out that later event initiating the earlier draft.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A payment followed by publication, without a first-draft date or causal evidence, leaves the initiation claim unresolved.

v02-style-authors-fact.justification: The comparison does not determine whether these texts actually have the same or different authors.

verdict_examples.supported: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning every selected A text to Ada and every selected C text to distinct person Bea would establish different authors for this specified corpus.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning both selected sets to the same sole author would negate different authorship for this corpus.
verdict_examples.insufficient: The small, genre-confounded comparison without authenticated authorship links leaves both same-author and different-author possibilities open.

v02-style-evidence.justification: The supplied description identifies an uncalibrated descriptive comparison with material sample and genre confounds. It cannot establish human attribution. Rejecting this sufficiency claim does not establish a common author.

verdict_examples.supported: A materially different analysis with independently established authorship evidence sufficient for this corpus could establish different authors; capitalization differences alone would not.
verdict_examples.contradicted: The fully described, uncalibrated and confounded comparison cannot establish different human authors.
verdict_examples.insufficient: If the contents and validation of a claimed authorship analysis were not supplied, whether that analysis establishes the conclusion could remain unresolved.

v02-authors-different.justification: The stipulated accurate, corpus-specific sole-authorship acknowledgments establish distinct authors without style inference.

verdict_examples.supported: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning every selected A text to Ada and every selected C text to distinct person Bea would establish different authors for this specified corpus.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning both selected sets to the same sole author would negate different authorship for this corpus.
verdict_examples.insufficient: The small, genre-confounded comparison without authenticated authorship links leaves both same-author and different-author possibilities open.

v02-authors-same.justification: A single stipulated sole author for both complete selected sets directly negates different authors for this corpus. This does not generalize to unlisted posts.

verdict_examples.supported: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning every selected A text to Ada and every selected C text to distinct person Bea would establish different authors for this specified corpus.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Accurate authenticated public authorship records assigning both selected sets to the same sole author would negate different authorship for this corpus.
verdict_examples.insufficient: The small, genre-confounded comparison without authenticated authorship links leaves both same-author and different-author possibilities open.

v02-indirect-not-direct.justification: Institutional funding and employment do not establish a direct D-to-P transfer, but neither rules one out.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated public settled-payment record identifying D as direct payer and P as direct payee within the specified period would support the transfer claim.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A demonstrably complete, authenticated public register covering every direct D-to-P transfer in the exact period, with no entries, would negate that bounded claim.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A D-to-institute grant and P employment, without a direct transfer record or exhaustive exclusion, establish neither a direct payment nor its absence.

v02-direct-settled.justification: The evidence directly establishes the amount, parties, settlement date and purpose in the exact transfer proposition.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated accurate settled-transfer disclosure matching D, P, USD 5000, 2026-09-01 and Report R supports this specific transfer.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A complete authenticated settlement record showing that the specified transfer never settled would negate this claim; a different unrelated payment would not.
verdict_examples.insufficient: An unsigned pledge or an unverified payment screenshot alone would leave this exact settled-transfer claim unresolved.

v02-direct-transfer-excluded.justification: The stipulated complete bounded register excludes the exact claimed transfer. It does not exclude other relationships.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated public settled-payment record identifying D as direct payer and P as direct payee within the specified period would support the transfer claim.
verdict_examples.contradicted: A demonstrably complete, authenticated public register covering every direct D-to-P transfer in the exact period, with no entries, would negate that bounded claim.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A D-to-institute grant and P employment, without a direct transfer record or exhaustive exclusion, establish neither a direct payment nor its absence.

v02-absence-incomplete.justification: An incomplete search cannot establish absence, and its incompleteness does not establish a payment either.

verdict_examples.supported: A demonstrably complete authenticated register for all direct D-to-P transfers in the exact period, showing none, supports this bounded absence claim.
verdict_examples.contradicted: One authenticated settled direct D-to-P transfer within the period contradicts the absence claim.
verdict_examples.insufficient: No matches in incomplete registers establish neither universal absence within the period nor the existence of a payment.

v02-absence-complete.justification: Explicitly complete coverage supports only this bounded absence finding. It supplies the detection basis missing from the incomplete-search case.

verdict_examples.supported: A demonstrably complete authenticated register for all direct D-to-P transfers in the exact period, showing none, supports this bounded absence claim.
verdict_examples.contradicted: One authenticated settled direct D-to-P transfer within the period contradicts the absence claim.
verdict_examples.insufficient: No matches in incomplete registers establish neither universal absence within the period nor the existence of a payment.

v02-copied-origins.justification: All three articles derive from blog B, with no independent firsthand account supplied. The claim counts repetitions as independent origins.

verdict_examples.supported: Three verified reports based on three distinct firsthand witnesses, with established independence, would support the count.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Three reports explicitly derived from the same original blog, with no independent verification, negate three independent firsthand accounts.
verdict_examples.insufficient: If sourcing and independence of the three articles were unknown, their count alone would not settle the independent-origin claim.

v02-account-continuity.justification: The same stable numeric account ID establishes account continuity across these captures, without authenticating a human.

verdict_examples.supported: Two genuine captures with the same stable account ID and different handles establish account continuity.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Genuine captures with two distinct stable account IDs negate the claim that they show the same account, without determining human identity.
verdict_examples.insufficient: Unverified screenshots with missing account IDs leave account continuity unresolved.

v02-offensive-authorship.justification: The offensive content is established at the account level. The similar display name does not establish personal authorship by Ada or its negation.

verdict_examples.supported: An authenticated accurate public acknowledgment by Ada identifying post 777 as her own work would support personal authorship.
verdict_examples.contradicted: Reliable authenticated public evidence assigning sole authorship of post 777 to a different person would negate Ada personally writing it.
verdict_examples.insufficient: A genuine account-level post plus a similar display name, without a human authorship link, leaves Ada attribution unresolved.
